audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats Tongue Lash as an ability that simply stuns — 'his Q tongue stun' in early, mid, late, spikes[3], wants.you[2], wants.foe[0] and whys[0]. The three-stack gate that actually arms the stun is never mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: This is the decisive mechanic of the matchup and its absence makes every threat line in the entry unreadable. Tongue Lash only stuns a champion who ALREADY carries three stacks of An Acquired Taste; otherwise it damages and slows. Stacks come from any damaging hit, so the stun is not random — it is a counter Mel can watch fill. Right now the entry tells her to fear a stun on every Q, which means she cannot tell the safe Q from the lethal one, and she will play the whole lane at the wrong distance.
audit.corrected: An Acquired Taste stacks on every Tahm Kench hit. At three stacks Tongue Lash stuns and consumes them — count the stacks, not the Q.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Q Tongue Lash: 'If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed')
champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (P An Acquired Taste: 'Damaging enemy champions builds stacks')

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text says the stun 'chains into W devour', wants.foe[0] says 'chain devour', and mid says 'he lands Q into W devour'. Devour is Tahm Kench's R. His W is Abyssal Dive.
audit.why: Wrong slot on the ability that kills you. A Mel player watching his W bar for Devour is watching the wrong cooldown — and the full layer separately, and correctly, tracks Abyssal Dive as W, so the two layers disagree with each other about what W does. Devour is also gated behind the same three stacks as the stun, which is the piece that makes the whole threat legible: three stacks means he can either stun you or eat you.
audit.corrected: Devour is R and needs three An Acquired Taste stacks on the target. Abyssal Dive is W, the knockup gap-closer on 21s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (R Devour: 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion'; W Abyssal Dive cd 21/20/19/18/17, flags knockup, zone)

audit.whatIsWrong: Grey health is attributed to his passive throughout — whys[4] 'before his passive can regenerate the health', wants.you[1] 'before his passive regenerates', plus 'grey-health passive' in wants.foe[1].
audit.why: Grey health is Thick Skin (E), not An Acquired Taste (P). The distinction is not cosmetic: Thick Skin has an ACTIVE that converts all stored damage into a shield immediately, on a 3 second cooldown. That is a burst-absorb Mel must play around, and it directly defeats the entry's core plan of stacking Overwhelm and detonating Golden Eclipse. Believing it is a passive regeneration teaches the player to detonate whenever she likes; knowing it is a 3s-cooldown active tells her to bait the shield first.
audit.corrected: Thick Skin (E) stores damage and can be cashed into an instant shield on a 3s cooldown — force it out before you detonate.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (E Thick Skin cd 3, flags shield/heal, 'Active: Convert all stored damage into a temporary shield')

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t all say Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'. breakdown.cooldowns names Abyssal Dive as the matchup-defining cooldown but never gives its duration.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26 — twenty seconds is below the floor at rank 5 and barely half the rank-1 value. Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1, which is the actual length of the window the entry keeps telling the player to wait for.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal is gone 38s at rank 1; Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] tells the player to 'avoid a random tongue stun' at level 1.
audit.why: Tahm Kench cannot stun anyone at level 1 until he has landed three damaging hits to build the stacks. There is no random level-1 stun to avoid. Teaching the player to respect a threat that cannot exist yet costs her the free CS and the free poke the rest of the entry says level 1 offers.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Tongue Lash damages and slows; the stun needs three stacks first.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Q Tongue Lash, P An Acquired Taste)

edits.before: You win the straight-up lane all game — he cannot out-damage your stacked poke and execute, and his grey-health sustain only stretches the lane, it never wins it. Keep your distance, never let a Q tongue stun walk onto you in a sidelane, and let your ranged passive keep chunking — but ward for his roams so a held lane never becomes a lost game elsewhere.

notes: UNVERIFIED CLAIM I DELIBERATELY STOPPED REPEATING: wants.you[2] says 'Hold W to eat his Q tongue projectile and fire it back, denying his only gap-close stun'. Two problems. First, the kit does not flag Tongue Lash as a projectile (its flags are hardCC, slow, heal), while it does flag genuinely reflectable spells elsewhere in the library — so whether Rebuttal reflects Tongue Lash is unconfirmed and I would not assert it either way without a wiki check. Second, Tongue Lash is not his gap-closer; Abyssal Dive (W) is. I left wants.you[2] untouched rather than guess, but I removed the same unverified reflect claim from content.early while rewriting that string for the stack mechanic, so the entry no longer teaches it in two places. Worth a wiki confirmation on Tongue Lash's projectile status — if it does reflect, wants.you[2] should be rewritten to say so precisely and to name Abyssal Dive as the actual gap-closer. WORTH KNOWING: Thick Skin's 3-second active shield is a much bigger obstacle to Mel's stack-and-detonate plan than anything the entry previously described, and it appears in the missing-interactions file for this matchup. I have put it into five strings across both layers. The full layer had the W slot right (Abyssal Dive) while the content layer had it wrong (called Devour 'W') — the two layers disagreed with each other, not just with the kit.
